title: Packaging: local build and verification > 2. Config summary
lines: apps/kira-studio/build/config.yml is the source from which Wails generates build assets.

In build/config.yml, info.productName is "Kira Studio" and info.productIdentifier is "com.kirathecat.kira-studio"; the Wails build is the only build now, so the earlier deliberately-distinct "-shell" identifier from P51/P52 is gone (P57 D11).
info.version in build/config.yml is the app's version and the only place a version is defined.
The dev_mode section of build/config.yml drives `wails3 dev`: watched extensions, ignore lists, and the three dev commands.
After editing info in build/config.yml, run wails3 task common:update:build-assets to regenerate assets; this overwrites hand edits under build/, so Info.plist is regenerated, not hand-maintained.

build/darwin/Info.plist has CFBundleName and CFBundleExecutable "Kira Studio", CFBundleIdentifier com.kirathecat.kira-studio, CFBundleIconFile icons, and scaffolded version 0.0.0 in the source plist; the bundle's copy of the version is stamped at packaging time.
LSMinimumSystemVersion is 14.0.0, hand-narrowed from Wails' template default of 12.0.0, matching the build's MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET/CGO_* flags and the README's macOS 14+ product claim.
After running wails3 task common:update:build-assets, re-narrow the macOS minimum version in both plists, because the template hardcodes 12.0.0 and the run reverts them.

The macOS floor is 14 rather than 13 because Go 1.27 builds its own objects for macOS 13 minimum; a lower -mmacosx-version-min only yields a linker warning that the object file was built for a newer macOS than is being linked.

title: Packaging: local build and verification > 2. Config summary > Where the version comes from
lines: build/config.yml's info.version is the single source of the app version; everything else is stamped from it at build time.

The Go binary gets its version because apps/kira-studio/Taskfile.yml's APP_VERSION reads config.yml and BUILD_FLAGS links it in via -ldflags -X …/internal/buildinfo.Version=<version>, in both dev and production branches.

The About dialog version is carried in main.go's application.Options.Description, because the macOS About item (application.About role) is rendered by Wails with name, description and icon but no version field of its own.
AppService.Info()'s appVersion reads buildinfo.Version; nothing in the renderer calls it today, so it is API surface, not a display path.

Info.plist's CFBundleShortVersionString and CFBundleVersion (read by Finder's Get Info) are set by create:app:bundle running PlistBuddy on the bundle's copy after cp; the checked-in plist keeps scaffolded 0.0.0 because it is generated and hand-edits would not survive common:update:build-assets.
An unlinked build (go run, go test, go build ./... by hand) reports internal/buildinfo's literal 0.0.0-dev, which distinguishes it from a real build.
verify-packaging.sh check A5 asserts the packaged bundle's CFBundleShortVersionString equals config.yml's info.version, so a bundle built around a stale plist fails.
The PlistBuddy step no longer skips silently off macOS: guarded by -x /usr/libexec/PlistBuddy, its else branch hard-fails create:app:bundle with a "broken macOS environment" error.
The root package.json's version is not the app version; it is npm metadata for a private, unpublished workspace root and nothing in the app or build reads it.
darwin:package:dmg is what bun run package:studio invokes: deps package, then create:dmg.

create:dmg runs wails3 tool package --format dmg over the built .app with background darwin/dmg-background.png, volume and file icon darwin/icons.icns, window 540×380; the tool adds the /Applications symlink and places the icons itself; macOS only.
darwin:package has deps build, then create:app:bundle, and can be called on its own to get just the bundle.

darwin:build → build:native is preconditioned on uname -s = Darwin with no off-macOS branch; deps are common:go:mod:tidy, common:build:frontend, common:generate:icons; it runs go build -tags production -trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags="-w -s" with GOOS=darwin CGO_ENABLED=1 GOARCH=$ARCH (host arch unless overridden) and MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=14.0.

create:app:bundle rm -rfs any previous bundle, creates Contents/{MacOS,Resources}, copies icons.icns, Assets.car (if present), the binary and Info.plist, and ends with codesign:adhoc. The rm -rf is needed because other steps only copy into the bundle, so stale resources would otherwise outlive the build that stopped producing them.

common:build:frontend runs the same bun run build:studio as the earlier checklist; Task's sources/generates up-to-date checking makes the second invocation a no-op, so building the renderer first is cheap insurance.
scripts/sign-bundle.sh does ad-hoc signing, runs by bun run package:studio after the Task pipeline, is macOS only and exits 1 elsewhere.

title: Packaging: local build and verification > 2. Config summary > Where the version comes from
lines: The macOS bundle needs only one deep codesign over the whole bundle, because there is no nested vendored Node binary or Kafka native module to sign individually any more.
create:app:bundle already runs codesign --force --deep --sign -; sign-bundle.sh re-signs and then verifies, which is redundant but harmless; it is the script a human or CI invokes.

create:app:bundle signs the bundle before create:dmg copies it into the image, so the .app inside the .dmg is already signed; sign-bundle.sh's later re-sign of the outer .app cannot reach inside a built image and does not need to.
The .dmg image itself is signed with a plain codesign --force --sign -, deliberately without --deep, because a disk image is a flat file with no bundle tree to recurse into.

The Taskfile tasks darwin:sign, darwin:sign:notarize (wails3 tool sign [--notarize], Developer ID), darwin:build:universal and package:universal are deliberately present but not wired into any package.json script.
Signing and notarization are deferred past v1 by SPEC.md §3, and the app is arm64-only, so a universal binary has nothing to be universal across.
Credentials are encrypted under an AES-256-GCM key held in a macOS Keychain generic-password item (service "Kira Studio Secrets"), implemented in apps/kira-studio/internal/secrets/keyring_darwin.go.

Keychain ACLs are keyed to a stable code-signing identity, which ad-hoc signing lacks, so the first launch after installing a new build may show one Keychain access prompt; Always Allow answers it permanently for that build. This is accepted, not worked around with a bundled private key.
The credential-reveal confirmation gate (internal/localauth) calls LAContext.evaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthentication) to confirm the device owner before decrypting a saved password for display.

It is an open question (P14 F7 item 1) whether an ad-hoc-signed bundle may present the LAContext.evaluatePolicy prompt; this is unconfirmed on real hardware, and the answer is to be recorded in §6.3 of docs/HISTORY.md (v1.1 P14).

If an ad-hoc-signed bundle cannot present the LAContext prompt, the app falls back to the in-app confirmDialog() as on Linux, and macOS Touch ID confirmation would then be a Developer-ID-signing-only capability.

title: Packaging: local build and verification > 5. Off-macOS: what this environment could actually check
lines: The Wails packaging pipeline compiles a real Go binary with CGO_ENABLED=1 against macOS system frameworks, so it cannot produce a bundle on Linux, unlike the replaced electron-builder pipeline.
The previous electron-builder pipeline assembled a complete, inspectable .app on Linux by downloading prebuilt Electron binaries, and only failed at the macOS-only sips step for dmg.
build:native requires macOS: darwin:build has a precondition on uname -s = Darwin and no off-macOS branch.
codesign does not exist off Darwin and there is no fallback; every step calling it is behind the Darwin precondition, and sign-bundle.sh deliberately exits 1 off macOS.

Off macOS, scripts/verify-packaging.sh with no bundle prints one "skipped A1/A3/A5/N2" note and one "skipped A4/N3" note and passes on the static checks alone; even with a bundle it skips A1/A3/A5/N2 for want of codesign/PlistBuddy.
A green verify:packaging on Linux proves only the static checks (S1/S2/S5/S6/S7/S8/S10/S11/S12), not that any bundle is correct; A1/A3/A5/N2 need the real .app.
Off macOS, everything that feeds the bundle is fully verifiable: the renderer build, typecheck, lint, the Go unit tests, and the static half of verify:packaging.

title: Packaging: local build and verification > 7. CI, releases, install and update
lines: The .github/workflows/ directory holds two workflows: pr.yml and release.yml.
db-compat.yml and test-matrix.yml were folded into release.yml's own jobs; see docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
pr.yml (formerly named CI, renamed to match what it gates) runs on push/PR to main plus workflow_dispatch.

title: Packaging: local build and verification > 7. CI, releases, install and update
lines: There is no package-smoke job; the bundle assertion lives only in release.yml's "Assert packaged bundle and disk image" step, because it checks the actual tagged release build rather than a merge-to-main run at a possibly different commit.

The checks job's test:go step runs on macos-15 without Docker and exercises only the driver-independent half of apps/kira-studio/internal/adapters/*/*_test.go; Testcontainers-backed tests skip with a named DockerUnavailableMessage when no Docker daemon answers.
Full-coverage test:go needs a runner with Docker, which is what the container-tests job is for.

P58f D1 moved per-engine DB coverage from packages/db-fixtures/ specs into apps/kira-studio/internal/adapters/*/*_test.go without changing which runner exercises it; Electron-hosted macOS runners have neither Docker nor nested virtualization.
Releases are cut by manually pushing a tag vX.Y.Z (release.yml triggers on v*.*.*, one tag for both apps, direct publish); nothing creates or pushes tags.

The release build job writes the tag (minus its v) into both apps' build/config.yml info.version in its own checkout, so no pre-tag version-bump commit is needed, and asserts both writes landed before building.

On a release tag, ci-gate, build (macOS), test-matrix (Linux) and db-compat (Linux, min|max) start together with no needs between them; ci-gate waits for a green pr.yml run on the tagged sha or dispatches one (scripts/release-ci-gate.sh).
The release build job restores the setup action's caches from main and saves none, because tag-scoped caches are never restored by a later tag.

The release build runs package:studio and package:space, names the images kira-studio-macos-arm64.dmg and kira-space-macos-arm64.dmg, runs verify:packaging and the bundle/disk image assert, hashes both and uploads them as artifact release-dmgs.
lint and typecheck do not rerun in release.yml; ci-gate proves PR CI ran them on the tagged sha.

The publish job (ubuntu) runs only when every other job passed; it re-checks artifact hashes, refuses a tag that already has a published release, creates a draft with both images, verifies each asset (state, size, sha256 digest), then publishes with one API call.
A failed gate leaves no release and no draft, and a failure after the draft exists deletes the draft.
A published release is public at once and /releases/latest serves it; the §4 real-hardware checks run after publish against the published assets.

If a post-publish check fails, ship a fixed next patch tag, because the updater offers only strictly newer versions; the bad release may optionally be deleted so /releases/latest falls back to the previous one. Installed copies are not downgraded.

For a flaky failed release gate use "Re-run failed jobs"; for a real failure delete the tag (git push --delete origin vX.Y.Z), fix, and tag again; if PR CI is red on the sha, fix or rerun PR CI first, then rerun the release's failed jobs.

Silent auto-update is deferred past v1 by SPEC.md; the user-initiated install/update via scripts/install.sh (P119) is not silent. macOS silent auto-update also requires a signed and notarized app, which §6 still defers.
verify-packaging.sh check S1: no electron-updater/update-electron-app dependency in package.json.
verify-packaging.sh check S2: no updater code in apps/ or packages/.

Check S5: package.json's package:studio/package:space scripts must still run wails3 task darwin:package:dmg (so the shipped .dmg always exists to upload); the check fails if an entry point is swapped for something that could publish.

Check S6: frontend/dist/assets/*.js must not contain the Playwright debug-hook identifiers (__kiraCount, __kiraCacheStats, __kiraRetention, __kiraRetainedBytes, __kiraTreeConnectionIds), because Task's build:frontend fingerprint ignores dist and could skip rebuilding after test:ui:studio wrote a hooks-enabled bundle.
S6 checks frontend/dist rather than the .app bundle so it also runs on Linux and before packaging.
Check S7: frontend/src/main.ts assigns no window.__kira* outside its if (__KIRA_DEBUG_HOOKS__) block.
Check S8: apps/kira-studio/main.go calls no os.Getenv at all.
Check S10: no reference to browser_download_url or releases/download under apps/, packages/ or internal/; scripts/ is excluded because scripts/install.sh is the one sanctioned downloader.
The embedding-model download (P210) is a user-clicked app-code download from a Hugging Face resolve/ URL with a pinned SHA-256, not a release asset, so S10 stays green.
Never download native code at runtime; the ONNX Runtime dylib is fetched at build time by scripts/fetch-onnxruntime.sh.

Check S11: scripts/install.sh must exist and pass sh -n, its line-2 marker (# kira-install-contract: 1) must match the constant in internal/appupdate/install.go, raw.githubusercontent.com must appear exactly once across apps/, packages/, internal/ (InstallScriptURL), and shellcheck runs on the script when on PATH.

Check S12: ORTVersion in internal/memory/embed/paths.go must equal ORT_VERSION in scripts/fetch-onnxruntime.sh, and create:app:bundle in apps/kira-space/build/darwin/Taskfile.yml must reference libonnxruntime.<version>.dylib.
There is no publish provider, update feed, latest-mac.yml or .blockmap; they are absent by construction.

A tagged release build polls GitHub's releases/latest API for vlad-cirstean/kira-studio (via shared internal/appupdate, no gh CLI dependency) and, when the tag is newer, shows a status-bar item opening a dialog with an Update button.

On Update click, the app re-checks availability, then internal/appupdate.Installer fetches scripts/install.sh fresh from main (never bundled), validates its contract marker, and spawns it detached with --app=studio|space; after hand-off over an fd the app quits and the script swaps the bundle into /Applications and reopens it.
Nothing downloads or installs without the user's explicit click; S10/S11 keep the app-code half true and scripts/install.sh is the sanctioned exception.
A dev/test build (buildinfo.Version of 0.0.0, 0.0.0-dev or 0.0.0-unknown) makes no update request and refuses InstallUpdate outright.
Because release.yml goes through a draft and /releases/latest excludes drafts and prereleases, a failed run never shows up to the update check.
A future silent auto-update would require, in order: code signing and notarization, a SPEC.md scope change reversing "no silent auto-update", then an update feed and background-updater wiring.

scripts/db-compat.sh (bun run test:compat) runs per-engine conformance packages against each kind's oldest and newest supported server image, sixteen (kind, min|max) pairs, outside test:go and pr.yml because it is too expensive per push.

The standalone db-compat.yml workflow is gone; release.yml's db-compat job runs it (min and max in parallel) and every release tag must pass it before publish. One-off runs use bun run test:compat -- --only <kind> --min|--max locally.
scripts/test-matrix.sh (P25's auth/config tier) likewise moved into release.yml as a job rather than a standalone workflow.
Any commit touching .github/workflows/*.yml requires the GitHub OAuth workflow scope, which is why P19/P20 workflow changes were staged in plan folders until a session with that scope applied them.

title: Packaging: local build and verification > 8. Kira Space packaging
lines: Kira Space embeds two gitignored bundles, frontend/dist (desktop UI) and frontend/dist-mobile (phone app); both must exist before go build.
Since P223 the frontend/dist-mobile embed (go:embed all:frontend/dist-mobile) contains only index.html, favicon.ico and assets/, with no service worker, manifest or setup page.
The Taskfile build:frontend task builds both bundles (bun run build then bun run build:mobile), so packaged builds embed the real phone app.
On a clean checkout or fresh worktree, sh scripts/prepare-worktree.sh builds both frontend bundles; in CI, bun run build:space chains both builds.

As of v1.9 P100, Kira Space is a separate app with its own bundle, DMG and copy of the pipeline (apps/kira-space/build/config.yml, apps/kira-space/Taskfile.yml, apps/kira-space/build/darwin/Taskfile.yml), with CFBundleIdentifier com.kirathecat.kira-space.
bun run package:space is the entry point for packaging Kira Space: it runs wails3 task darwin:package:dmg in apps/kira-space, then sh scripts/sign-bundle.sh apps/kira-space "Kira Space".
sign-bundle.sh takes the app dir and app name as $1/$2 (since P100 Part 2), so one script signs both apps' bundles instead of a near-identical copy per app.
Kira Space packaging produces apps/kira-space/bin/Kira Space.dmg, Kira Space.app and the bare binary Kira Space.
As of P119, Kira Space.dmg ships as kira-space-macos-arm64.dmg on the same release as Kira Studio's disk image: one release.yml build job, one tag, one release, with no separate release-space job.

darwin:package and darwin:package:universal depend on fetch:onnxruntime (scripts/fetch-onnxruntime.sh osx-arm64), which downloads the MIT-licensed ONNX Runtime release tgz, SHA-256 pinned, into gitignored apps/kira-space/build/onnxruntime/osx-arm64/.

create:app:bundle copies libonnxruntime.1.29.1.dylib into Contents/Frameworks/ and its LICENSE and ThirdPartyNotices into Contents/Resources/, before codesign:adhoc, and fails loudly if the dylib is missing.
The ONNX Runtime dylib is arm64-only because ORT 1.29.1 has no x86_64 macOS build, so the universal bundle's x86_64 slice reports embeddings unavailable.
Bundling ONNX Runtime adds about 43 MB to the Kira Space bundle.
memory-embed is the same executable run as a subcommand, so no extra binary needs signing.

Mac verification of the ONNX bundling is a human item: Contents/Frameworks/libonnxruntime.1.29.1.dylib must be present, codesign --verify --deep --strict must pass, and worker footprint in Activity Monitor must be at most 150 MB.
build:native needs macOS, and codesign does not exist off Darwin, so Kira Space packaging cannot be built or signed on Linux.
